title: flow readiness: a time-relative start whose objectName differs from timeRelative.object declares an object its run never binds
body:
domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Cbvcmv8YWFhFJwzjKL

Filing gate: ② a contradiction the flow schema admits and the runtime resolves silently, found by the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of PR #30276 (#30026), record 6649920800, should-fix 3. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade.
Reader: `domain:server`, the flow readiness rules (`validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts`, beside `flow-time-relative-descriptor-invalid`).
Dedupe: `timeRelative.object objectName`, `flow-time-relative-descriptor-invalid` → none open. **New.**

## What happens

A time-relative flow's start may name `config.objectName` and `config.timeRelative.object` as two different objects. The run sweeps `timeRelative.object` (`time-relative-trigger.ts` finds rows of `desc.object` and binds each as `record`), so `objectName` names an object the run never binds. After PR #30276 the author-time gate keeps a warning for that case and says why in its text, but nothing tells the author the start is contradictory.

## Wanted

- [ ] A readiness verdict on a time-relative start whose `objectName` is set and differs from `timeRelative.object`, naming both and the fix (drop `objectName`, or make them equal). Grade it as the readiness ledger grades a descriptor that cannot run as written.
- [ ] Declare it as the narrowing it is if it refuses (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` precedent: #30015, #30276).

Links: #30026, PR #30276, PR #30015.
